whyExpo.substatement: Building an energy future that is sustainable and disaster-resilient.
paragraphs: Nepal's energy sector is entering a pivotal phase. Hydropower capacity has grown to approximately 4,145.7 MW, with a national target of 30,000 MW by 2035 — expanding beyond domestic power needs toward industrial growth, electric mobility, renewable energy, and cross-border power trade with India and Bangladesh.

But this growth is now being tested. Recent flash floods and debris flows have damaged hydropower projects across the country, exposing the vulnerability of energy infrastructure to climate-related disasters. The sector's future depends not only on scaling capacity, but on building it to withstand a changing climate.

Since 2018, the Himalayan Hydro Expo has connected key stakeholders across four editions through 2024. Himalayan Green Energy Expo 2027 marks the next chapter, expanding this established platform into a broader green-energy forum, while placing resilience at the center of the conversation.

card1.title: Pharping Powerhouse
card1.description: Nepal's clean energy journey commenced in 1911 AD with the commissioning of the 500 kW Pharping powerhouse, Asia's second hydropower plant.

card2.title: Sovereign Clean Power Target
card2.description: Scaling from 4,145.7 MW existing capacity towards the 30,000 MW national target by 2035 AD — expanding beyond domestic power needs toward industrial growth, e-mobility, and regional power trade.

editions.desc: Inaugural gathering of Nepal's independent hydropower developers — the beginning of an annual industry platform.
International technology pavilions expanded. Chinese, Indian and European OEMs joined Nepal's growing energy floor.
Post-pandemic return marked a surge in energy sector investment interest and regional trade discussions.
Ministerial plenary, tri-nation power export framework discussions, and 250+ exhibitors across 3 days.

ippan.subtitle: INDUSTRY KNOWLEDGE
ippan.title: Independent Power Producers' Association, Nepal
ippan.description: Established in 2001, IPPAN is a non-profit, non-government autonomous organization established to encourage private-sector participation in Nepal's hydropower sector. It serves as a link between private power developers and government organizations, while supporting the exchange of technology, expertise, knowledge, financial and management information among independent power producers.

eventSolution.description: Founded in 2014, Event Solution Nepal is an event management company focused on creating and delivering events from planning through execution. Its services include event planning and consulting, event management and coordination, event production and setup, event rentals, logistics and event operations, and sound, lighting and LED solutions.
